title: Hanford treats 2.3 billion groundwater gallons in FY 2024, the tenth year above 2 billion
publisher: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Environmental Management
summary: DOE reports 2.3 billion gallons treated in FY 2024 and ten consecutive fiscal years above 2 billion gallons, while Washington Ecology later reports more than 38 billion gallons cumulatively across six facilities. Denominator: FY 2024 sitewide treated groundwater volume across Hanford's six treatment systems, plus a ten-year threshold series; the later regulator cumulative total is a separate denominator.
key_findings: Finding: DOE reports 2.3 billion gallons treated in FY 2024 and ten consecutive fiscal years above 2 billion gallons, while Washington Ecology later reports more than 38 billion gallons cumulatively across six facilities.
Denominator: FY 2024 sitewide treated groundwater volume across Hanford's six treatment systems, plus a ten-year threshold series; the later regulator cumulative total is a separate denominator.
Boundary: A threshold series does not disclose the exact annual value for every year.
Boundary: Treated water volume is not annual contaminant mass removed, plume reduction, or aquifer restoration.
Boundary: The 200 West capacity expansion is capability and cannot be counted as realized treatment beyond the reported 2.3 billion gallons.
Next action: Add exact annual facility-level volumes, uptime, contaminant mass, concentration, plume extent, energy, cost, regulator review, and accepted expansion performance.
